reason: 'tap' only occurs as part of 'tap root' / 'tap-rooted'; PO_0020127 primary root has 'tap root' as an EXACT synonym. Same rule as the previous review's 'taprooted' (C345).

label: pseudoverticillate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of lateral structures by virtue of their being inserted singly, but so close together on a short stretch of the axis that they appear whorled.
reason: Floras contrast this with truly whorled leaves, so it must not map to PATO:0001951 whorled. PATO:0000619 crowded (overfilled) misses the 'looks like a whorl' part. Sibling of PATO:0001951 whorled.
'Setae scarce', 'albumen peu abondant' and 'lateral roots peu abondantes' all mean few or little. PATO_0001997 has 'decreased number' as an EXACT synonym.

Syncarpous means the carpels are fused with one another, i.e. like parts united: FLOPO connate on the carpels. When the word is said of the fruit, ovary or flower, the bearer should move to the carpels.
Same as the previous review's rule for 'palmately compound' (C304): leaflets radiating from one point = PATO digitate.

label: sour
definition: A flavour quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a sharp, acid taste like that of lemon juice or vinegar.
reason: PATO has PATO:0002474 bitter under flavourful but no sour. This is the taste of fruit pulp. FLOPO:0991019 sour-smelling is a smell and lists 'sour' only as a RELATED synonym, so the two must be told apart by context.
Pithy stems are filled with pith, in contrast to hollow ones ('pleines de moelle', 'with a continuous pith'). PO_0006109 pith has 'medulla' as a synonym.
'Inflorescence panicled' / 'en panicules' says the inflorescence is a panicle, which is the PO class itself. FLOPO:0991198 panicle-like stays for things that only resemble a panicle.

It says a part stays whole (not torn, split or decayed), usually about how it persists ('persisting more or less intact'). It means nothing without the damage it is contrasted with. PATO's 'intact' terms are about reproductive status.
Bulbiform = bulb-shaped, which is an EXACT synonym of PATO bulbous (a teardrop-like 3-D shape).

Most uses ('distally knobbed' glands, cells 'terminating in a distinct knob') mean a tip abruptly enlarged into a rounded head, which is FLOPO head-shaped. Surfaces with many knobs (trunk, seed) fit PATO_0002427 knobbled better.
Crisp margins and leaves are crisped (finely curled), as the previous review did for 'crispate' (C361). The French 'crissant' (crunchy bark) is a different sense and should not take this rule.
Most examples are French 'sarmenteux', meaning long flexible stems that scramble or climb by leaning. FLOPO climbing includes plants that lean on supports. Same treatment as 'lianescent' (C354).

label: sympodial
definition: A branched quality inhering in an axis by virtue of its growth being continued by a series of lateral branches, each of which takes over when the apex of the one before it stops growing.
reason: A standard botanical branching type (rhizomes, stems, inflorescences) with no PATO term. Its opposite, monopodial, is also missing and could be added beside it.
Stunted / 'rabougri' = abnormally small, which matches PATO dwarf-like (EXACT synonym 'dwarfed').
Nectariferous = bearing or producing nectar, i.e. having a nectary. Treated like 'lenticellate' (C204).

It describes a sudden change (abrupt apex, neck, apiculus, sheath transition) and means nothing without the shape it modifies. Where a fixed meaning exists it is already covered by values like FLOPO:0991054 mucronate.
A comparison stated without the part it is compared with, like 'shorter' and 'narrower' in the previous review.
An adverb that sets the degree of another quality ('densely farinose', 'densely hirtellous'). It is not a quality by itself.
Ecarunculate = seed without a caruncle. Treated like 'ebracteate' (C206).

target: sour (the new class proposed for 'sour' in this batch)
reason: 'Pulp acid', 'acidulée' describe a sour taste, not a measured pH. PATO_0001429 acidic is the pH of a solution, so the word should be a synonym of the new 'sour' class.
Too vague: 'modified' needs what the part has become ('petals modified to nectaries'), and that is a different statement.
The negation of PATO decurrent, like 'unlobed' = not lobed (C239).
Well-defined veins, teeth, zones and alar cells are clearly visible. Same reading as 'distinct' for veins (C176).
Pronounced midveins, nerves, ribs and lobes stand out from the surface, which matches PATO prominent (standing out or projecting). Some uses only mean 'clearly visible' (conspicuous).

label: saprophytic
definition: A trophic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its lacking or nearly lacking chlorophyll and getting its nutrients from dead organic matter, usually through fungi associated with its roots.
reason: A way of feeding common in flora habit statements, with no PATO term. Probably outside PATO's scope, like epiphytic, so keep it in FLOPO. 'Mycoheterotrophic' is the modern name for the same plants.
Hippocrepiform = horseshoe-shaped, which is a synonym of PATO U-shaped.
Said of a set of like parts (stamens, sepals, lobes) whose members are the same size, which is FLOPO equal. When a second part is named ('as long as the sepals'), pattern 10 applies instead.

label: gelatinous
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being soft, moist, somewhat translucent and jelly-like.
reason: Used for arils, mesocarps and seed appendages. PATO has only PATO:0000387 soft and PATO:0000998 viscous, and neither gives the jelly-like texture.
A vague impression of strong growth ('vigorous plant', 'rameaux vigoureux') with no clear form to annotate. PATO:0002310 robust (thick, sturdy) would be a guess.
